answer:
I found four problems in the uncommitted changes. I only read the diffs of the two `lib` files. I didn't open the modified test files or run anything.

1. **`lib/core/AxiosHeaders.js:129`: the CR/LF check is gone.** The old code threw `Invalid character in header content` when a header value contained a newline. Now `headers.set('X', 'a\r\nInjected: 1')` quietly sends `aInjected: 1`. That hides the bug and changes the value. Rejecting the value is safer than rewriting it, and anything that expects the throw will break.
2. **`lib/core/AxiosHeaders.js:8`: the new regex silently deletes valid characters.** It removes everything above 0xFF and every control character except tab. A value like `日本語` or `Привет` is emptied or truncated with no warning. A value like `a\x00b` becomes `ab`.
3. **`lib/core/AxiosHeaders.js:42`: every header value is now trimmed.** Leading and trailing spaces and tabs are removed. The old code only stripped trailing CR/LF, so `' x '` now becomes `'x'`. This goes beyond the scope of the change.
4. **`lib/helpers/shouldBypassProxy.js:108`: `NO_PROXY` now treats `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` and `::1` as the same host.** `NO_PROXY=localhost` now also bypasses the proxy for `127.0.0.1` and `[::1]`. Anyone who deliberately proxies one of those, such as to a tunnel, loses that route. The match also ignores the rest of `127.0.0.0/8`, so it's inconsistent.

findings.summary: The CR/LF validation that threw on invalid header values was removed. Invalid characters are now stripped silently, so callers get no error.
findings.failure_scenario: headers.set('X', 'a\r\nInjected: 1') used to throw 'Invalid character in header content'. It now sends 'aInjected: 1', which hides the bug and changes the value. Code or tests that expect a throw break. The change is also a security-posture regression, because rejecting the value is safer than mutating it.

findings.summary: INVALID_HEADER_VALUE_CHARS_RE strips every character outside Latin-1 (above 0xFF) and every control character except tab, with no error. Valid non-Latin-1 values are silently corrupted.
findings.failure_scenario: A header value such as 'filename=日本語.txt' or 'Привет' is reduced to an empty or partial string and sent without warning. The old code kept these values and let Node decide what to do. Stripping control characters from inside the value also merges tokens, so 'a\x00b' becomes 'ab'.

findings.summary: sanitizeHeaderValue now trims leading and trailing spaces and tabs from every header value. The old code only stripped trailing CR/LF.
findings.failure_scenario: Values that rely on exact whitespace now change. For example, a value of ' x ' becomes 'x'. This is a behavior change beyond the intended scope. It also affects values read back through AxiosHeaders.get.

findings.summary: All loopback names are now treated as equivalent for NO_PROXY matching. An entry for one loopback name (localhost, 127.0.0.1 or ::1) now bypasses the proxy for the other two, which is broader than the user configured.
findings.failure_scenario: NO_PROXY=localhost makes requests to http://127.0.0.1:8080 and http://[::1] skip the proxy. A user who deliberately proxied 127.0.0.1, for example to reach a tunnel, loses that route. The match also ignores the rest of the 127.0.0.0/8 range, so the equivalence is inconsistent.
